faqs.question: Can my landlord keep my deposit because of Halloween decorations?
faqs.answer: Only for damage beyond normal wear and tear, and the line depends on where you live. Idaho's Attorney General table counts nail and pin holes as normal wear but unapproved paint colors as damage. In England and Wales a protected deposit stays in the scheme while you dispute any deduction.

faqs.question: Do removable adhesive hooks damage rental walls?
faqs.answer: They can lift paint, especially fresh or matte paint, so treat them as the riskiest no-hole option. Stay under the weight rating on the pack, test one in a hidden spot for 24 hours, and pull it off exactly as the instructions show.

faqs.question: Can I put a wreath or pumpkin outside my apartment door?
faqs.answer: Only if your building runs a 'managed use' policy for the common parts and management agrees. UK fire guidance for blocks of flats makes 'zero tolerance', with nothing left in corridors, the default. Ask in writing before anything goes on the corridor side of your door.

faqs.question: Do I need my landlord's permission to decorate for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Not for freestanding decor inside your own home, but you do for anything that fixes to walls, doors or railings if your lease restricts alterations. A short email naming the method and the end date, such as 2 November, gets you a written answer you can keep.

faqs.question: How do I hang Halloween lights in an apartment without nails?
faqs.answer: Use battery string lights draped along an existing curtain rail, a tension rod or a bookshelf. Never run a cable under your front door into the corridor, because UK fire guidance tells landlords to stop residents wiring decorative lights into common parts.

faqs.question: What should I photograph before decorating a rental?
faqs.answer: Photograph the exact wall, door or window you will use, with the date showing, before you start. Take the same shot after the decor comes down, so any later deduction can be compared against both.

faqs.question: What is the easiest small space Halloween decor?
faqs.answer: A frame swap: slide a printed Halloween poster in front of art that already hangs on an existing hook. It makes no new mark and takes about 5 minutes per frame to undo.

faqs.question: Is it safe to put Halloween decorations on a balcony?
faqs.answer: On a private balcony, yes, if everything sits below and inside the railing so wind cannot carry it off. Escape balconies and shared access decks count as common parts, so keep them clear like a corridor.

faqs.question: Can I draw on my apartment windows for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Glass markers usually wipe off plain glass with a damp cloth in about 10 minutes. Test a corner first, and skip windows with a film or tint you cannot identify.

faqs.question: Can a SubhSandesh Halloween page invite my whole building?
faqs.answer: No. Both Halloween templates are one-person greeting pages, built for a partner, best friend, family member or child. For a building, a note from management or a lobby sign works better.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Decorations for Apartments That Leave No Trace

Halloween decorations for apartments work best when they hang from what is already there, stay inside your own front door and come down without a mark: tension rods, existing picture hooks, magnets, glass markers and weight-rated removable hooks. Shared hallways are usually off limits, because UK fire guidance for blocks of flats makes "zero tolerance" in corridors the default policy. When the person you most want to impress will never see your living room, the decor has to travel by phone instead: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, at an average of 11.1 views per page.

Below: US and UK deposit rules, corridor rules, six no-hole methods compared, balconies and a three-zone layout. Halloween is always 31 October, a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027.

## What makes a Halloween decoration apartment-safe?

An apartment-safe Halloween decoration leaves nothing a landlord could call damage, sits inside the space your lease gives you, and adds no flame or wiring to shared areas. In practice it hangs, stands, clips or sticks with something designed to come off cleanly.

The line between wear and damage is set by state law, not by taste. Idaho Legal Aid publishes an [Idaho Attorney General table on normal wear and tear](https://www.idaholegalaid.org/sites/default/files/What%20is%20Normal%20Wear%20and%20Tear%20Guide.pdf) under Idaho Code Section 6-321: nail holes, pin holes and small cracks in the wall count as normal wear, while gaping holes in plaster and walls painted a color the landlord did not approve count as damage. Other states draw the line elsewhere, so check your own before trusting a thumbtack.

## Your deposit: what US and UK rules count as damage

In England and Wales, the [GOV.UK tenancy deposit protection guide](https://www.gov.uk/tenancy-deposit-protection) says a landlord must put your deposit in a government-approved scheme within 30 days, and return it within 10 days of you both agreeing how much comes back. You get it back if you meet the tenancy terms, pay rent and bills, and do not damage the property. As of October 2026, assured periodic tenancies have replaced assured shorthold tenancies, a change dated 1 May 2026.

In a dispute the deposit stays in the scheme until it is sorted, so evidence matters. The Idaho guide tells tenants to photograph the empty unit at move-in and move-out, with dates on the photos. Do the same for the wall you decorate, before 1 October and after 1 November.

Many renters hesitate to ask at all. In [a 2022 UK study built on 58 interviews about life in poor-quality housing](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC9347395), Brown and colleagues found that many tenants were afraid to ask landlords even for flexibility on rent, in case it antagonised them and ended the tenancy. A one-line email asking to use removable hooks inside your front door until 2 November is a far smaller ask, and a written yes is evidence.

## Hallways and front doors: the fire rule most renters miss

Shared corridors are escape routes. The Home Office guide [Fire safety in purpose-built blocks of flats](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/65e9def95b6524001af21bcc/Fire_Safety_in_Purpose_Built_Blocks_of_Flats_Guide-update.pdf), written in 2011 for England and Wales and still published with a note that it is no longer comprehensive, says unrestricted use of common parts "is clearly not acceptable". Buildings choose between "zero tolerance", where residents keep nothing in the common parts, and "managed use", which might allow door mats, pot plants and framed pictures.

Zero tolerance is the guide's default. It should always apply where the escape stair is combustible or the building cannot support a "stay put" evacuation policy, and normally where flats open straight onto a stairway. A skeleton propped in the corridor can break that policy even if your lease never mentions Halloween.

Flat front doors are meant to be fire-resisting and self-closing, so nothing you hang on yours should stop it shutting and latching on its own; open it fully and let go to test. The guide also tells landlords to stop residents running wiring from their flats to decorative lights in the common parts. In the US the equivalent rules sit in your city's fire code and your building's house rules, so ask the management office before anything goes on the corridor side of your door.

## 6 ways to hang Halloween decor in a rental without holes

Each method covers four things in a fixed order: where it works, what it holds, mark risk and undo time. Times are our estimates, October 2026.

### 1. A tension rod across an inside doorway

It works across a doorway between two rooms or inside a window recess and holds a light fabric panel such as a black voile curtain cut into ragged strips you walk through. Mark risk is low, because pressure holds the rod, not screws. Undo time is about 2 minutes.

### 2. Swap the art, not the wall

It works on any frame already hanging on an existing hook, holding a printed Halloween poster or a public-domain engraving of bats slid in front of the current picture. Mark risk is nil, since no new fixing goes in. Undo time is about 5 minutes a frame.

### 3. Magnets on a steel door or fridge

It works on the inside face of a metal-skinned front door, a fridge or a steel shelf, holding thin magnetic sheet cut into bat, cat or crescent-moon silhouettes. Mark risk is nil on paint, but keep the closer, hinges, seals and any safety sign uncovered. Undo time is about 1 minute.

### 4. Glass markers on one window

It works on a street-facing window or a glass balcony door, holding a drawn harvest moon, a row of rooftop cats. Mark risk is low on plain glass, but test a corner and skip any window with a film or tint you cannot identify. Undo time is about 10 minutes with a damp cloth.

### 5. Weight-rated removable hooks

It works on smooth, fully dried paint or inside a cupboard door, holding only what the pack's weight rating allows, such as a string of paper moths. Mark risk is medium, so test one hook in a hidden spot for 24 hours and remove it exactly as the pack shows. Undo time is about 10 minutes.

### 6. The bookshelf graveyard

It works on one shelf at eye level, holding books turned spine-in with paper tombstone labels tucked into the pages, a little dried moss and a flameless LED candle. Mark risk is nil, because nothing is fixed to anything. Undo time is about 5 minutes.

## Rental decor methods compared: mark risk, corridor use and undo time

This table groups the six methods, plus the tempting thumbtack. The columns are what a landlord or fire assessor checks.

| Method group | Mark risk (Idaho wear-and-tear test) | Corridor side of your door? | Undo time (our estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tension rod, frame swap, bookshelf | None to low: no new holes | No, these stay inside | 2–5 min each |
| Magnets inside a steel door | None | Only under "managed use", with written OK | 1 min |
| Glass markers on a window | Low on plain glass | Not applicable | 10 min |
| Removable hooks | Medium: can lift fresh paint | Not under "zero tolerance" | 10 min |
| Thumbtacks or small nails | Normal wear in Idaho; other states vary | No | 15 min, plus filler if required |

Three of the five rows carry no realistic mark risk. Nothing here belongs in a zero-tolerance corridor.

## Balconies: what a small outdoor space can hold

A balcony can be part of the escape plan. The same fire guide lists "barbecues on access decks and escape balconies" among the extremes landlords battle, and a deck shared with neighbors counts as common parts. If people pass your balcony to leave the building, treat it like a corridor.

On a private balcony, keep everything below the top of the railing and inside it, so a gust cannot drop a pumpkin onto someone underneath. If your lease has a clause on railings, that clause decides. Otherwise one battery lantern on the floor reads from the street after dark on 31 October.

## Small-space layout: a three-zone plan for a studio or one-bed

Small space Halloween decor works by subtraction; decor on every surface of a studio reads as clutter. Pick three zones: the first thing you see from the front door, one surface at eye level and one window.

- **Studio:** the doorway curtain on the kitchen or bathroom opening, the bookshelf graveyard, one marker window.
- **One-bed:** a frame swap in the living room, magnet silhouettes inside the front door, one marker window.
- **Shared flat:** agree zones in writing with roommates before 1 October, one shared spot each plus your own room.

Three zones also give you three photos. Keep them for the move-out file and the page below.

## When the lease says no: a greeting page that leaves no mark

SubhSandesh's Halloween templates greet one person; they are not party invitations, building notices or hallway decor. They suit a renter whose lease rules out most of the above. [The interactive Halloween card with photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is the quick option, roughly 5 minutes to build, with room for six photos, a pumpkin they carve to reveal your word and a letter lit by their flashlight.

[The cinematic premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) needs roughly 10 minutes and carries more: twelve photos, a voice note of up to a minute, an unlock time if you want one and a box for their reply. Across SubhSandesh, 38.5% of creators add a password before sharing, and 90.9% of started pages get published.

If the flat holds two people comfortably and you would rather show the decor in person, an [invitation page they must answer](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better. Their yes starts a countdown to the evening you planned.

## When apartment decorating, or a greeting page, is the wrong choice

Skip hooks entirely if your move-out inspection lands in early November; dated photos protect you, but no fixing at all protects you more. In a zero-tolerance building nothing goes outside your door, whatever the neighbors do.

The pages lose too. Each greets one person, so it does nothing for a lobby, a trick-or-treating child or a building party, and the interface is in English only. For a roommate, decorating the shelf together on 30 October beats any link.

## Sources

- GOV.UK, "Tenancy deposit protection", undated: https://www.gov.uk/tenancy-deposit-protection
- Brown et al., "Locked down", Journal of Community Psychology, 24 May 2022: https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC9347395
- Home Office, "Fire safety in purpose-built blocks of flats", July 2011: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/65e9def95b6524001af21bcc/Fire_Safety_in_Purpose_Built_Blocks_of_Flats_Guide-update.pdf
